strategy.thesis: aMoon is Israel's largest dedicated healthtech/life-sciences investor; its Growth vehicle backs mid-to-late-stage biopharma, medtech, diagnostics and digital-health companies at the convergence of technology and biology, investing in growth rounds, pre-IPO rounds and companies in pivotal clinical trials, while sister vehicle aMoon Velocity covers earlier stages.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Runs 'aMoon Alpha', an in-house platform providing portfolio companies talent, strategic-partnership and market-intelligence support.

summary.en: aMoon is a Ra'anana-based healthtech and life-sciences investment platform; its growth-stage vehicle (aMoon Growth) funds mid-to-late-stage biopharma, medtech, diagnostics and digital-health companies through growth rounds, pre-IPO rounds and pivotal-trial financings.

sources.title: aMoon Fund
sources.supports: HQ location, two-vehicle structure (Velocity/Growth), sector focus, notable public portfolio companies
sources.quote: we invest in early and late-stage companies pursuing disruptive, cutting-edge solutions for high unmet medical needs.

sources.title: aMoon's second healthtech fund tops out at $750 million
sources.supports: aMoon Growth II fund size of $750M
sources.quote: aMoon II, which launched in April 2018, finalized $660 million in investor commitments, and the second fund ultimately reached $750 million in commitments, which was its maximum allowed cap.

sources.title: Israel health fund aMoon 2 raises $660 million in investor commitments
sources.quote: aMoon II invests in mid- to late-stage life science companies in the field of digital health, medical technologies and biopharmaceuticals that operate in Israel as well as other health-tech hubs like the US and Europe.

verification_notes: Founder attribution is inconsistent across sources: the official site credits Yair Schindel, MD, MBA and Tomer Berkovitz, PhD, while some press describes Marius Nacht (Check Point co-founder) as co-founder/anchor backer; exact total AUM (reported elsewhere as $1.1B-$1.3B) is not disclosed on the official site, so it was omitted. Included in the growth-crossover slice on the strength of the dedicated aMoon Growth vehicle, which explicitly targets growth/pre-IPO rounds.

strategy.thesis: ALIVE is a mid-to-late-stage HealthTech growth investor backing advanced-stage medical device, digital health and bio-convergence companies that are ready to scale, commercialize and lead global markets, leveraging a strategic-partner ecosystem of hospital chains, HMOs and financial institutions.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Exclusive ecosystem of strategic partners comprising leading hospital chains, HMOs and financial institutions to support clinical and commercial expansion of portfolio companies.

summary.en: ALIVE is a pioneer mid-to-late-stage Israeli HealthTech growth fund investing in Israeli and international medical-device and digital-health companies at advanced growth stages, operated through ALIVE One (advanced clinical/early commercial) and ALIVE Growth (growth-stage) vehicles.

sources.quote: ALIVE announced the initial closing of ALIVE Growth Fund III, a $180-200M growth-stage HealthTech fund investing in Israeli and international mid-to-late stage Medical Device and Digital Health companies.

verification_notes: Fund naming varies slightly across sources (ALIVE Growth vs. ALIVE Growth Fund III); treated as the same growth vehicle. hq_city not confirmed from sources reviewed and left blank.

strategy.thesis: CBI is a TASE-listed (largest) Israeli life-sciences holding company investing across the full company lifecycle from seed to maturity, in both privately held and publicly traded biotechnology, pharmaceutical, diagnostics and medical-device companies -- including growth-capital and PIPE rounds -- typically as lead investor taking a board seat.

summary.en: Clal Biotechnology Industries is Israel's largest life-sciences holding company, publicly traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE: CBI), investing across seed through growth/PIPE stages in both private and public biotech, pharma, diagnostics and medical-device companies.

Portfolio company count (~13, reported in secondary sources) also omitted pending primary-source confirmation.

strategy.thesis: Pontifax is a Herzliya-based healthcare-dedicated investor spanning company formation through late-stage clinical and growth-equity rounds; its portfolio ranges from preclinical biotech to publicly traded pharmaceutical companies, and it runs a dedicated venture-debt fund used to finance private crossover rounds when valuations exceed its equity fund's comfort range.

summary.en: Pontifax is a Herzliya-based, healthcare-dedicated investment firm with roughly $1.2B under management that invests across the full biopharma/medtech/digital-health lifecycle, including late-stage growth-equity and crossover rounds via a dedicated venture-debt vehicle, with a portfolio spanning preclinical biotechs to publicly traded pharma companies.

sources.title: Pontifax investing $150M venture debt fund alongside crossovers
sources.supports: $150M venture debt fund used for private crossover rounds; $250M equity fund closed April 2018
sources.quote: The fund will invest in private crossover rounds when valuations are outside our comfort range for the equity fund. As mezzanine rounds have grown larger, some private companies' valuations have grown out of reach for Pontifax's $250 million equity fund, which closed in April 2018.

sources.title: Due to high demand for biotech, Pontifax crosses $1.3 billion funding threshold
sources.supports: Pontifax portfolio spans biopharma, medtech, digital health across ~100 companies
sources.quote: Its portfolio spans three sub-sectors - Biopharma, MedTech, and Digital Health

verification_notes: Founded-year (2004) and total AUM ($1.2B) figures come from reputable secondary sources (CBInsights/Golden, Pontifax's own site) rather than a single dated primary filing, but are consistent across sources. Classified primarily as 'vc' because Pontifax's core identity is a multi-stage healthcare VC; flagged with crossover-fund/growth-equity as subtypes given its explicit growth-equity and crossover/public-portfolio activity, which is why it is included in this growth-crossover slice.

strategy.thesis: OrbiMed invests across the global healthcare industry from seed-stage venture capital through growth equity to large publicly traded companies; it opened a dedicated Herzliya, Israel office in 2010 (operating as OrbiMed Israel Partners) to source and support Israeli biopharma, medical-device, diagnostics and life-science companies through its venture, private-equity/growth and public-equity strategies.

summary.en: OrbiMed is a global healthcare investment firm (HQ: New York) that opened a dedicated Herzliya, Israel office in 2010; through its venture, private-equity/growth and public-equity strategies it backs Israeli healthcare device, pharmaceutical, biotechnology and oncology companies from seed through crossover/public stages.

sources.title: About - OrbiMed
sources.supports: Multi-stage seed-to-public strategy; Herzliya office opened 2010; broad private-equity/growth-equity strategy
sources.quote: OrbiMed invests across the global healthcare industry, from seed-stage venture capital to large publicly-traded companies.

sources.title: About - OrbiMed
sources.supports: Herzliya, Israel office opened 2010; broad private-equity/growth strategy
sources.quote: OrbiMed's private equity strategy is broad and flexible, investing from start-ups through growth equity.

sources.quote: OrbiMed Israel Partners is a venture capital fund managed by OrbiMed, located in Herzliya, Israel, and targets investments in the healthcare device, supply, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, life science and oncology sectors.

verification_notes: OrbiMed's true global headquarters is New York, NY (founded 1989); included in this Israel-region slice because it operates a dedicated Herzliya office and Israel-focused fund vehicle (OrbiMed Israel Partners) opened in 2010, per the region-inclusion rule for foreign firms with a dedicated regional arm.
